name: Metallic Bellows Expansion Joints
oneLineScope: Metallic bellows expansion joints to EJMA and ASME B31.3, 80 – 8,000 mm NB circular

specTable.value: axial · lateral · angular, per EJMA design

types.name: Single
types.description: One bellows absorbing axial movement in a straight run.

types.name: Universal
types.description: Two bellows with centre spool for large lateral movement.

types.name: Tied lateral
types.description: Tie rods restrain pressure thrust; absorbs lateral offset.

types.name: Hinged
types.description: Angular rotation in one plane; used in sets of two or three.

types.name: Gimbal
types.description: Angular rotation in any plane via a gimbal ring.

types.name: Pressure-balanced elbow
types.description: Balances pressure thrust at a change of direction.

types.name: Inline pressure-balanced
types.description: Balances pressure thrust in a straight run.

types.name: Externally pressurized
types.description: Pressure applied to the bellows OD; suits high axial travel.

faqs.question: Which design codes do you design metallic bellows expansion joints to?
faqs.answer: Metallic bellows expansion joints are designed and engineered to the EJMA (Expansion Joint Manufacturers Association) standards and ASME B31.3 piping code requirements. Under special conditions FEA analysis is carried out.

faqs.question: What size range of metallic expansion joints do you manufacture?
faqs.answer: Circular metallic bellows from 80 mm to 8,000 mm nominal bore, and rectangular bellows up to 9,000 mm × 5,000 mm — manufactured at the Vitthal Udyognagar works, Anand, Gujarat.

faqs.question: What types of metallic expansion joints do you supply?
faqs.answer: Single, universal, tied lateral, hinged, gimbal, pressure-balanced elbow, inline pressure-balanced and externally pressurized expansion joints — selected to absorb axial, lateral, angular or combined movements per the EJMA design method.

faqs.question: Which bellows materials can you work with?
faqs.answer: Stainless steel grades SS 304, 304L, 316, 316L, 321 and 310; nickel alloys Inconel 600 and 625, Incoloy 800 and 825, and Hastelloy; and duplex materials.

faqs.question: Which industry sectors do you supply expansion joints to?
faqs.answer: Oil & gas, refineries & petrochemicals, fertilizers, power & energy, steel, cement, ship building, cross-country pipelines, sugar, dairy, paper and the Department of Atomic Energy. Precise Engineers is an EIL-approved unit, established 1994.
